title: Weighted Job Scheduling
statement:
Given `n` jobs where job `i` runs over the half-open time interval `[startTimes[i], endTimes[i])` and pays `profits[i]`, return the maximum total profit obtainable from a subset of non-overlapping jobs.

Contract
- `startTimes`, `endTimes`, and `profits` have the same length `n >= 0`.
- For every job `i`, `0 <= startTimes[i] < endTimes[i]` and `profits[i] >= 0`.
- Two jobs `[s1, e1)` and `[s2, e2)` do not overlap if `e1 <= s2` or `e2 <= s1`: a job starting at the exact time another finishes is allowed.
- Return `0` when there are no jobs.

Examples
- `starts = [1, 2, 3, 3]`, `ends = [3, 4, 5, 6]`, `profits = [50, 10, 40, 70]` -> `120` (choose jobs `[1, 3)` and `[3, 6)`).
- `starts = [1, 2, 3, 4, 6]`, `ends = [3, 5, 10, 6, 9]`, `profits = [20, 20, 100, 70, 60]` -> `150` (choose `[1, 3)`, `[4, 6)`, `[6, 9)`).
- `starts = [1, 1, 1]`, `ends = [2, 3, 4]`, `profits = [5, 6, 4]` -> `6`.
hints: Greedy selection by earliest end time or highest profit fails because one high-profit job can overlap two smaller jobs whose combined profit is larger (or vice versa).

Sort the jobs by end time. Define dp[i] as the maximum profit using the first i sorted jobs. For job i, either skip it (dp[i - 1]) or take it plus dp[p], where p is the count of sorted jobs that end at or before job i's start time.
Because end times are sorted, find p with binary search in O(log n) per job. Intended complexity: O(n log n) time, O(n) space.
inputSyntax: Input: s-e:p, ... (comma-separated start-end:profit jobs), for example: 1-3:50, 2-4:10, 3-5:40, 3-6:70
